_instructions: Score every hint for the pair it sits under. 'already_served' is context only: do not score it.

hints.explanation: The film Alien was sold with the tagline "In space no one can hear you scream", because sound cannot travel through the near-vacuum of space.

lines.ALIEN: Alien's famous tagline is about a scream no one can hear.
lines.VACUUM: Sound needs air to travel, so a scream makes no sound in a vacuum.

hints.explanation: In The Very Hungry Caterpillar, the caterpillar starts by eating through one apple.

lines.APPLE: On Monday, the hungry caterpillar eats through one apple.
lines.CATERPILLAR: The Very Hungry Caterpillar is Eric Carle's picture book.

hints.explanation: Gimli is the axe-wielding dwarf in The Lord of the Rings.

lines.DWARF: Gimli is the dwarf of the Fellowship.

hints.explanation: Romeo woos Juliet at her balcony and later drinks poison.

lines.BALCONY: Romeo speaks to Juliet in the famous balcony scene.
lines.POISON: Romeo drinks poison in the tragic ending of Romeo and Juliet.

hints.explanation: Archimedes is said to have shouted "Eureka!" in his bath while testing a gold crown, and "Eureka" is California's motto from its gold rush.

lines.BATH: Legend says Archimedes cried "Eureka!" in his bath.
lines.GOLD: California's motto, "Eureka", recalls the discovery of gold there.

hints.explanation: Royal jelly is a food made by worker honeybees.

lines.JELLY: Larvae raised as queens are fed royal jelly.

hints.explanation: Bird watchers use binoculars.

lines.BIRD: Bird watchers use binoculars to spot birds.
lines.WATCH: You watch faraway things through binoculars.

hints.explanation: A plank is a long board, and in stories pirates make captives walk the plank.

lines.BOARD: A plank is a long, flat board.
lines.PIRATE: In pirate stories, prisoners are forced to walk the plank.

hints.explanation: You can break a bone, and athletes try to break a record.

lines.BONE: A broken bone is called a break or fracture.
lines.RECORD: Setting a new best mark is called breaking the record.

hints.explanation: Pinky and the Brain are cartoon lab mice, and the pinky is the little finger.

lines.BRAIN: The Brain is the scheming mouse in Pinky and the Brain.
lines.FINGER: The pinky is the smallest finger on the hand.

hints.explanation: Herbie is the Volkswagen Beetle star of Disney's The Love Bug.

lines.LOVE: Herbie's first film is The Love Bug.

hints.explanation: Icing is also called frosting, and a cake is topped with it.

lines.CAKE: A cake is often covered in icing.
lines.FROST: Icing is another word for frosting.

hints.explanation: Graduates wear a cap and gown, and a gown is a long, formal dress.

lines.CAP: The graduation outfit is a cap and gown.
lines.DRESS: A gown is a long, formal dress, like a ball gown.

hints.explanation: Princess Jasmine rides Aladdin's magic carpet, and jasmine rice is a fragrant rice.

lines.CARPET: In Aladdin, Jasmine flies on the magic carpet.
lines.RICE: Jasmine rice is a fragrant long-grain rice.

hints.explanation: GOAT stands for Greatest Of All Time, a title fans give their favorite champions.

lines.CHAMPION: Fans call their favorite champion the greatest of all time.
lines.GOAT: In sports talk, GOAT means Greatest Of All Time.

hints.explanation: Dove is a brand of chocolate and a brand of soap.

lines.CHOCOLATE: Dove chocolate is made by Mars.
lines.SOAP: Dove soap is sold as a beauty bar.

hints.explanation: In Monsters, Inc., monsters reach children through closet doors, and Boo is the little girl who follows Sulley back; boo is also what a monster shouts to scare you.

lines.CLOSET: In Monsters, Inc., monsters enter bedrooms through closet doors.
lines.MONSTER: Boo is the girl the monsters meet, and "boo" is the classic scare.

hints.explanation: Starbucks coffee is named after Starbuck, the first mate in Moby-Dick.

lines.COFFEE: Starbucks coffee takes its name from Starbuck.
lines.WHALE: Starbuck is first mate on the ship hunting Moby Dick, the white whale.

hints.explanation: John Denver sang "Take Me Home, Country Roads".

lines.COUNTRY: John Denver's best-known song is about country roads.
lines.ROAD: Denver asks the country roads to take him home to West Virginia.

hints.explanation: Corona is Latin for crown, and coronaviruses are named for their crown-like ring of spikes.

lines.VIRUS: Under a microscope, coronaviruses look like they wear a crown.

hints.explanation: Opossums famously play dead when threatened.

lines.DEAD: A threatened opossum can go limp and appear dead.
lines.PLAY: Playing possum means pretending to be dead or asleep.

hints.explanation: When Google Chrome is offline, it shows a little dinosaur you can play as in a jumping game.

lines.DINOSAUR: Chrome's offline game stars a pixel T. rex.
lines.INTERNET: Offline means you have no internet connection.

hints.explanation: Bullseye is the center of a target and the name of Target's dog mascot.

lines.DOG: Target's mascot is a dog named Bullseye.
lines.TARGET: The bullseye is the center of a target.

hints.explanation: Martin Luther King Jr. gave the "I Have a Dream" speech in 1963.

lines.DREAM: "I Have a Dream" is Dr. King's most famous speech.
lines.KING: Luther is the middle name in Martin Luther King Jr.

hints.explanation: An Easter egg is a secret hidden in a video game or film, named after Easter egg hunts.

lines.EASTER: Easter eggs are hidden for children to find.
lines.SECRET: Game makers hide secret extras called Easter eggs.

hints.explanation: The Sugar Plum Fairy dances in The Nutcracker ballet.

lines.FAIRY: The Sugar Plum Fairy is a famous character in The Nutcracker.
lines.SUGAR: The Sugar Plum Fairy has a famous dance in The Nutcracker.

hints.explanation: In Charlotte's Web, a spider named Charlotte saves Wilbur the pig on a farm.

lines.FARM: Charlotte lives in the barn on the Zuckerman farm.
lines.SPIDER: Charlotte is a spider who writes words in her web.

hints.explanation: "That's a wrap" ends a day of filming, and plastic wrap is a thin film for covering food.

lines.FILM: Directors say "That's a wrap" when filming is done.
lines.PLASTIC: Plastic wrap is also called cling film.

hints.explanation: A Bunsen burner makes a flame in a science lab.

lines.FLAME: A Bunsen burner gives a steady gas flame.
lines.LAB: Bunsen burners are a classic piece of lab equipment.

hints.explanation: Making a gaffe is putting your foot in your mouth.

lines.FOOT: To put your foot in your mouth is to make a gaffe.
lines.MOUTH: A gaffe is an embarrassing slip of the mouth.

hints.explanation: A true friend sticks with you through thick and thin.

lines.FRIEND: A loyal friend stays close through thick and thin.
lines.THIN: Thick is the opposite of thin, and they pair up in "through thick and thin".

hints.explanation: A gauntlet is an armored glove, and Marvel's Infinity Gauntlet holds the Infinity Stones.

lines.GLOVE: A gauntlet is a heavy armored glove.
lines.MARVEL: Thanos wields the Infinity Gauntlet in Marvel stories.

hints.explanation: The Hulk is Marvel's huge green hero with enormous strength.

lines.STRONG: The Hulk gets stronger the angrier he gets.

hints.explanation: Tony Hawk is a skateboarding legend, and Tony the Tiger sells Frosted Flakes.

lines.HAWK: Tony Hawk is a famous skateboarder.
lines.TIGER: Tony the Tiger is the Frosted Flakes mascot.

hints.explanation: Swiss cheese has holes, and the Swiss Army knife is famous.

lines.HOLE: Swiss cheese is known for its holes.
lines.KNIFE: The Swiss Army knife folds many tools into one.

hints.explanation: In The Nightmare Before Christmas, Jack Skellington is a skeleton.

lines.JACK: Jack Skellington is the hero of The Nightmare Before Christmas.
lines.SKELETON: Jack Skellington is a skeleton, the Pumpkin King.

hints.explanation: Packing everything but the kitchen sink means bringing everything.

lines.KITCHEN: The saying is everything but the kitchen sink.
lines.SINK: In the saying, only the sink gets left behind.

hints.explanation: You click a link, often with a mouse.

lines.LINK: You click a link to open it.
lines.MOUSE: A mouse makes a click when you press its button.

hints.explanation: Elephants are said never to forget, and they have trunks.

lines.MEMORY: The saying goes that an elephant never forgets.
lines.TRUNK: An elephant's trunk is its long nose.

hints.explanation: In a typical honeybee hive, the queen is the mother of the colony.

lines.MOTHER: A hive's queen bee lays the eggs, so she is mother to the colony.
lines.QUEEN: The queen bee heads the hive.

hints.explanation: Peter Pan flies and Peter Parker swings on webs.

lines.PAN: Peter Pan is the boy who never grows up.

hints.explanation: In The Prince and the Pauper, two look-alike boys switch places.

lines.PRINCE: The prince trades places with a poor boy in The Prince and the Pauper.
lines.SWITCH: The prince and the pauper switch lives.

hints.explanation: An album is a record made up of tracks.

lines.RECORD: Albums were long sold as vinyl records.
lines.TRACK: Each song on an album is called a track.

hints.explanation: The Rolling Stones are a rock band, and stones are rocks.

lines.ROCK: The Rolling Stones are a classic rock band, and stones are rocks.
lines.ROLL: The band took its name from the Muddy Waters song Rollin' Stone.

hints.explanation: In SpongeBob SquarePants, Plankton keeps trying to steal the secret Krabby Patty formula.

lines.SECRET: Plankton schemes to steal Mr. Krabs's secret formula.
lines.SPONGEBOB: Plankton is the tiny villain of SpongeBob SquarePants.

hints.explanation: Snakes shed their skin, and a tool shed stores garden tools.

lines.SKIN: Snakes shed their old skin as they grow.
lines.TOOL: A tool shed is a small building for storing tools.

hints.explanation: Open sesame opens the cave of the forty thieves, and Sesame Street is a children's show.

lines.STREET: Sesame Street is the long-running children's TV show.
lines.THIEF: In Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves, open sesame opens the thieves' cave.
